page: Amazon Web Services g6e.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine is provisioned with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 45 GB of VRAM. Bundled local storage includes 250 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate extreme polarization driven by the dedicated accelerator. In large language model inference, the NVIDIA L40S yields top-tier performance within the top 10% of tested instances, reaching 13,365.51 tokens per second during prompt processing and 506.94 tokens per second during text generation on small 135M parameter models. For medium 7B parameter models, prompt evaluation achieves 6,130.77 tokens per second and text generation clocks at 134.56 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU and memory throughput reflect the modest 4-vCPU footprint. The instance registered weak benchmark tiers across multi-core Geekbench (3,790.0), multi-core stress-ng (5,979.57), and Redis SET throughput (4.7 million ops/sec), while single-core compute performance placed in the top 25% with a 2,991.88 stress-ng score.

The primary architectural tradeoff centers on pairing an enterprise-grade GPU with an entry-level CPU core allocation and 2 Gbps baseline networking. From a resource-efficiency standpoint, the instance is optimized for workloads that run primarily on GPU compute, making full use of the 45 GB VRAM and NVMe scratch disk without paying the operational cost overhead of a larger host CPU footprint. However, applications bound by host memory bandwidth, widespread multi-core CPU scaling, or continuous network streaming will encounter bottlenecks on this instance profile.

Amazon Web Services g6e.xlarge is ideally matched for small-to-medium parameter deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, graphics rendering, visual computing pipelines, and GPU-accelerated video transcode workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services g6e.xlarge is an accelerated computing virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, the instance delivers 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores), 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 250 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network link. Its core capability stems from an NVIDIA L40S Ada Lovelace GPU with 45 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results exhibit top-tier LLM inference execution, generating 134.56 tokens per second on 7B models and prompt ingestion exceeding 6,130 tokens per second. Conversely, host-bound metrics like multi-core CPU processing, memory bandwidth, and Redis transactions place in lower benchmark tiers due to the compact CPU complement. This instance serves workloads focused on AI inference, graphics processing, and compute-heavy GPU acceleration requiring dedicated VRAM capacity without excessive host CPU expenditure.
